response_status.description: Indicates the review status of the agent response. Use changes_requested when the output should be reviewed, corrected, or confirmed by the user. Use confirmed only when the handoff analysis is explicitly confirmed or stable after revision. Use cancelled only when the analysis is cancelled.

handoff_zone_candidates.description: List of candidate handoff zones identified as a separate analytical overlay over the workflow graph. These objects do not modify the graph and are not graph nodes.

handoff_zone_candidate_id.description: Stable unique identifier of the handoff zone candidate, for example hzc_001.

name.description: Short human-readable name of the candidate handoff zone.

handoff_summary.description: Concise explanation of the handoff candidate, describing what appears to pass from one party/context to another.

location_kind.description: Describes where the handoff is located relative to the graph. Use the most specific possible location. uncertain_multi_ref_zone is only a fallback when the exact location cannot be safely localized.

source_ref_ids.description: Graph references where the handoff starts, is triggered, or becomes visible. Values may refer to wfpoint_id, decision_gate_id, or outcome_id.

target_ref_ids.description: Graph references where the receiving party takes over, continues the work, or becomes responsible. May be empty when the handoff is attached to an outcome whose target branch has not yet been created.

boundary_ref_ids.description: Minimal graph area needed to represent the handoff candidate. Values may refer to wfpoint_id, decision_gate_id, or outcome_id.

from_party.description: The party, role, system, team, queue, organization, or context from which responsibility, control, information, work, or dependency appears to move.

party_kind.description: Normalized kind of the sending party. Use only predefined values.

party_label.description: Human-readable label of the sending party, for example clinical ward team, document validation system, or manual review queue.

organization.description: Organization associated with the sending party. Use unknown if it cannot be inferred.

party_detail.description: Additional detail about the sending party, its role, or why it is relevant to the handoff. Use unknown if it cannot be inferred.

context_description.description: Description of the sending party's operational context in this handoff.

to_party.description: The party, role, system, team, queue, organization, or context that receives responsibility, control, information, work, or dependency.

party_kind.description: Normalized kind of the receiving party. Use only predefined values.

party_label.description: Human-readable label of the receiving party, for example social worker, rehabilitation facility, external validation service, or manual review queue.

organization.description: Organization associated with the receiving party. Use unknown if it cannot be inferred.

party_detail.description: Additional detail about the receiving party, its role, or why it is relevant to the handoff. Use unknown if it cannot be inferred.

context_description.description: Description of the receiving party's operational context in this handoff.

transferred_responsibility_or_control.description: Describes what responsibility, ownership, authority, work responsibility, or process control moves from the sending party to the receiving party.

transferred_payload.description: Concrete objects, documents, information, metadata, cases, requests, tasks, physical objects, or other payloads passed through the handoff.

sender_expected_action.description: Expected action of the sending party in order to perform the handoff correctly, such as prepare, send, assign, submit, notify, transfer, route, or provide required information.

receiver_expected_action.description: Expected action of the receiving party after receiving the handoff, such as receive, review, process, accept, reject, validate, confirm, continue, resolve, respond, or pick up work.

handoff_nature_tags.description: Controlled semantic tags describing the nature of the handoff. Use the smallest accurate set of predefined tags.

why_candidate.description: Explanation of why this graph location is considered a candidate handoff zone.

localization_uncertainty.description: Explanation of uncertainty about where the handoff is located in the graph. Use null when the handoff is clearly localized.

confidence.description: Confidence level indicating how strongly the graph and available context support this handoff candidate.

clarification_questions.description: Concrete questions needed to resolve material ambiguity in the handoff analysis. Keep empty when no clarification is needed.

question_id.description: Stable identifier of the clarification question, for example btq_001 or hzq_001.

question.description: Concrete clarification question to ask the user. Avoid broad questions such as Can you provide more details?

why_needed.description: Explains why the answer is needed and what part of the handoff analysis it affects.

handoff_zone_candidate_ids.description: Ids of the handoff zone candidates related to this question. May contain one or more candidate ids.

blocks_next_pass.description: True if the missing answer prevents a safe or useful next pass. False if the analysis can continue with lower confidence or a reasonable assumption.
